newsitem.title: CHINA: Tientsin Marine plans new B share issue.
newsitem.headline: Tientsin Marine plans new B share issue.

text.p: Tientsin Marine Shipping Co said on Tuesday it planned to issue an additional 90 to 95 million B shares over the next year.
The plan was adopted by shareholders at a meeting on Monday and will be submitted to the securities authorities for approval, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
Proceeds will be used to buy four container ships with a capacity of 400 to 600 standard containers each, which are expected to cost the firm $45 million to $50 million, the statement said.
The company plans to fix the price of the new issue on the average price of its listed B shares in the 10 days before the issue, the statement said.
The firm has 90 million B shares listed on the Shanghai stock exchange, which made their debut in April last year. The shares closed at $0.58 on Monday.
Shareholders at the meeting empowered the firm's board of directors to execute the new B share issue, the statment said.
They also approved a proposal by the board to distribute no dividend for the fiscal year of 1996, it said.
The company posted a net profit of 97.472 million yuan in 1996, up 39.45 percent from 69.897 million yuan in 1995 based on domestic accounting standards.
The 1996 net was 113.459 million yuan based on international accounting stardards, the company said.
With its foreign currency B shares only listed in 1996, the firm's 1995 results were not internationally-audited.
